mode.rule: Writing renders light. A blog, article, newsletter or any card fronting written material uses the website palette, because it is the same reading surface. Everything else — podcast, YouTube, episode art, short-form, feed cards for non-writing assets — renders dark.

og_card.rule: Light is the default and the standard for blog, articles, newsletter and any card fronting written material: it matches the website, so the card and the page it opens are one surface. Dark is the exception, for an OG card fronting a non-writing asset (an episode, a video, a short).

blog_og.rule: Light is the default and the standard for blog, articles, newsletter and any card fronting written material: it matches the website, so the card and the page it opens are one surface. Dark is the exception, for an OG card fronting a non-writing asset (an episode, a video, a short).
blog_og.note: Keyed by SURFACE, not canvas. variantFor() deliberately does not resolve surface_aliases: dual-mode is a property of the surface. Aliasing briefly let byte_size inherit this permission and accept --mode dark, which the writing-renders-light rule forbids. byte_size and monthly_digest are absent from this block on purpose, so --mode dark throws on them.

dual_mode.note: Only blog_og and og_card are dual-mode. Writing surfaces (byte_size, monthly_digest) render light only.

mode.the_signal_dark_retired: RETIRED by Al 2026-09-18. The dark masthead is not a variant and not a permitted exception: it is withdrawn. Five issues shipped dark (101 to 105) and are not re-rendered, consistent with how shipped assets have been treated elsewhere in this system. The token reader already refused dark on this surface, so nothing in the resolution chain changes; what changes is that the dark mockup is deleted from the MO Design System page and compose_signal() is rebuilt light rather than kept as a dark composer.
mode.the_signal_mode: LIGHT, and light ONLY. Confirmed by Al 2026-09-18: light is the website standard for anything that is writing, and The Signal is writing. modeFor('the_signal') already returned light and the surface is deliberately absent from dual_mode, so --mode dark throws. TWO ARTEFACTS CONTRADICT THIS AND ARE THE DRIFT, not the rule: the masthead mockup on the MO Design System page rendered dark, and thumbnail_builder.py compose_signal() renders dark on the RETIRED palette. The token system was right before either was fixed.
mode.writing_surfaces_note: blog_og is dual-mode (light default, dark for an OG fronting a non-writing asset). byte_size and monthly_digest are NOT dual-mode and render light only, so --mode dark throws on them. That is deliberate: a byte-size is writing.

colour.dark_border_provenance: NEW IN 3.2.0, and the only invented value in this change. The dark set had no border or hairline token at all, so mo_diagram's arrow/card strokes (#4a6272, undeclared) had nowhere to map. Derived in-family by lightening dark-panel #1C3C45 along the same hue; it is decoration, not text, so the 4.5:1 rule does not apply. FLAGGED FOR RATIFICATION: Al has not approved this hex. usage_rules: teal #2F9E8D is a graphic colour on light, never body text. Use teal-deep for text and links.
soft is for light grounds only. On dark use on-dark-soft.
Semantic pairs differ by mode. Light uses the darkened set, dark uses the bright set. The meaning never changes.

One radial teal wash per canvas, 20 per cent on dark and 12 per cent on light. Never two. PERMITTED ON LIGHT — amended 2026-09-14 by Al, reversing the v3.1.0 "never on light" rule. Values in structure.wash; never hardcoded in a producer.

display.use: asset titles, H1, slide and cover titles
display.weight_note: 800, not 900. RULED 2026-09-14 by Al. Montserrat has no Black face in this estate and adding one means two more files normalised in two font trees, regressing on every refresh. ExtraBold reads as a display face at every size we ship (verified by render), and 800 retroactively legitimises the back catalogue, which was rendered in ExtraBold outlines throughout the mislabelled-font period. Montserrat Black gains weight largely by closing apertures, which costs legibility at thumbnail scale rather than buying it. EXCEPTION, if it is ever wanted: single words set very large, where closed counters read as deliberate mass. That is a documented exception, never a global return to 900.

heading.use: H2 to H4, card and slide titles

label.use: kickers, eyebrows, timestamps, figures, code. Every surface, including architecture diagrams.

rule.note: One weight. A heavier line must mean something.

wash.rule: ONE radial teal wash per canvas, in teal #2F9E8D, centred per surface. Never two. PERMITTED ON LIGHT at 12 per cent.

canvas.document: A4 portrait, 14mm sides and top, 16mm foot
canvas.og_card_note: 1200x630 is correct and has always been correct. If a card rasterises at 1600x840 the defect is in the PRODUCER, not here: sharp's default density is 72 and the kit passed 96, scaling every unitless SVG dimension by 96/72. Fixed 2026-09-14. Do not 'correct' this token to match a bad render.
canvas.hosting_rule: In-body images are UPLOADED to the publishing platform's own CDN, never hotlinked. A published post currently serves a diagram from raw.githubusercontent.com, which is not a CDN, is rate-limited, and breaks if the repo goes private or the file moves. Raised 2026-09-14.

png_output.rule: No `quality` option on PNG output. In sharp, quality implies palette: true, which quantises.
png_output.measured: 2026-09-14: cards rendered INDEXED with 25 to 28 colours; a vertical slice through the radial wash held only 5 to 7 distinct values, i.e. visible banding rings. Present since the kit was written — every card it ever produced is banded, dark worse than light.
png_output.fix: png({ compressionLevel: 9, palette: false }) — lossless truecolour.
png_output.size_expectation: MEASURED 2026-09-15 on the six evergreen renders: 39,430 to 53,997 bytes (mean ~50KB), RGBA truecolour, no palette. The indexed originals were 69,210 to 88,823 bytes, so the lossless files are SMALLER — roughly 30 per cent smaller, not larger.
png_output.ceiling: 1MB, as a smoke alarm rather than a target. Retained, but note it is now ~20x the real output rather than ~2x: it will only ever catch a producer emitting something absurd.
png_output.second_reason_for_the_sweep: The banding is independent of the palette flip, so the six evergreen winners need re-rendering for image quality as well as for mode.
png_output.note_on_writing_surfaces: byte_size and monthly_digest share the og_card canvas via surface_aliases. They are NOT dual-mode: writing renders light, so --mode dark throws on them. blog_og is dual-mode because an OG card can front a non-writing asset.
png_output.why_smaller: Inferred, not measured: sharp's palette quantiser appears to dither, and dither is high-frequency noise that defeats PNG's row filters, whereas a smooth truecolour gradient reduces to near-zero deltas and compresses very well. The OUTCOME is measured; this explanation is not.
png_output.corrected_estimate: A prior estimate of 290KB-575KB (4x to 8x) was recorded here and in the Content Management letter. It was reasoned from 'lossless is bigger' and never measured. It was wrong in the wrong direction and is corrected here rather than quietly dropped.
png_output.acceptance: FILE SIZE IS NOT THE ACCEPTANCE TEST. Read PNG byte 25: colour type 2 or 6 passes, colour type 3 (indexed) means the quantised producer is still in use. Size moved in the opposite direction to the prediction, so a size check would have read as a failure when the fix had worked.
png_output.alpha_note: Output is RGBA. All pixels are opaque, so this is harmless, but an OG card carries no transparency by design and the alpha channel is dead weight. Not changed, because it is measured to cost little and changing it is a new render of everything.

The Signal, byte-size, the Digest and blogs sit under Mastering Observability. Ruled by Al 2026-09-14, restating what The_Signal_Card_Standard.md already said and what v3.1.0 lost: §6 of the standard, §5 of the marks standard and this rule all described two parallel equal lanes with no parent. The file that declares itself canonical was the one that dropped the hierarchy.
lockup.name_trap: the_signal is the NEWSLETTER and is house lane. signal_drop is the PODCAST and is podcast lane. One word apart, opposite wordmarks. Al's 2026-09-14 ruling on the Digest, The Signal and byte-size covers the newsletter only.
lockup.prohibition: Metrics & Mayhem must NOT appear on a house asset. That name is reserved for the book and the podcast.

endorsement.rule: PER SURFACE, ruled by Al 2026-09-16. Not blanket. A surface absent from this block has NO endorsement and renders nothing, so one cannot be acquired by accident — turning one on is an edit here, never in a producer. House surfaces throw if asked: a house asset cannot endorse itself.
endorsement.wording_note: "FROM MASTERING OBSERVABILITY" claims a source, not a format — it stays true if the show changes shape. Design's wording, not Al's ruling; the ruling was which surfaces, not which words. Change it here if the phrasing is wrong.
endorsement.why_youtube_only: YouTube is where a cold viewer meets the podcast with no other context, so the parent brand has work to do. An episode square appears inside a feed the listener has already chosen, where the endorsement is noise. That is the distinction Al drew.

Al ruled PER SURFACE — YouTube yes, episode squares no. See lockup.endorsement. Previously recorded here as open, with the note that it changes every thumbnail, square, title card, bookend and video card; in the event it changes one of them.

marks.rule: Resolve a mark by NAME from this manifest. Never by searching the tree — a search finds logo-master.svg and favicon.svg, which predate the ring mark. If a mark is not listed here it does not exist yet.

ring_mark.role: House mark. Two hairline rings and a solid centre: the lens resolving on a signal.
ring_mark.crossover_rule: Below 40px use the small variant. The hairline rings disappear at favicon and avatar sizes; the small variant carries a 2px ring and a larger centre so the mark survives.
ring_mark.supersedes: The heavier crosshair treatment on new assets. Crosshair survives only as page chrome in long-form PDFs.
ring_mark.mono_rule: One colour, no opacity, 1.2px stroke so it holds at a single ink weight. For single-colour print, stamping, watermarks and any surface where the two-tone mark cannot be reproduced. Never use mono where the full mark will render.
ring_mark.og_card_rule: 80px on a 1200-wide og_card. RULED by Al 2026-09-16, replacing 44px. At LinkedIn's ~552px render width 80px lands near 37px, comfortably over the 24px floor in Logo_and_Marks_Standard §1; 44px landed near 20px, under it. Above crossover_px so the FULL variant is used. Full opacity — the mark carries its own ring opacity in the file, so a producer opacity double-applies it.
ring_mark.og_card_placement: TOP RIGHT, opposite the eyebrow, x = W-60-80, y = 40. It was bottom right in the footer at 44px. It had to move: the footer band is 78px tall (rule at H-78 to the H-40 baseline) and cannot hold an 80px mark, and enlarging the band would push the rule into the subtitle. Top right balances the eyebrow and gives the mark the presence Al asked for. Design's layout call, 2026-09-16 — flagged as a call rather than a consequence.

favicon.role: Browser tab, bookmark bar, home screen. The site icon.
favicon.ruled: Al picked mo_ring_mark_favicon_32.png on 2026-09-17 over the manifest small variant. Recorded here because it existed in NO manifest: nothing generated it, no standard described it, and its treatment appears in no other file. That is why the favicon question kept reopening — the good answer was undocumented, so each conversation rediscovered only the two documented-but-worse options.
favicon.treatment: TWO concentric rings, 2px stroke, teal #2F9E8D at 0.70, plus a solid centre dot in teal-deep #17695C, on an opaque light ground #F6F8F7. Distinct from BOTH manifest variants: the full variant has 1px hairlines at 0.28 that disappear below the crossover, and the small variant collapses to a single ring in flat teal-deep, which reads as a circle with a dot rather than as the ring mark.
favicon.why_not_the_small_variant: The small variant is correct for a mark sitting INSIDE another design at small size, where one ring is enough and simplicity wins. A favicon is the mark standing alone as the only brand signal on screen, so keeping the concentric idea matters more than absolute simplicity. Both are right for their own job; this is a third job.
favicon.ground: OPAQUE, not transparent. All four PNGs carry their own light ground, which is why they hold on dark browser chrome as well as light. Do not regenerate these with a transparent background.

files.ico: website/favicon.ico — 16 and 32 in one file. The 32 entry is the byte-identical payload of mo_ring_mark_favicon_32.png, not a re-encode. The 16 is a high-quality downscale of it.

favicon.measured_2026_09_17: Ground #F6F8F7 = light.ground exact and centre #17695C = light.teal-deep exact, in all four. Full-strength ring #6BB9AD = teal at 0.70 over ground, blend matching on all three channels — reached in the 180, 192 and 512. In the 32 NO ring pixel reaches full strength: 46 distinct values, all partial coverage, darkest #70BCAF at 0.67. So for the 32 the ring colour is teal by inheritance from its build family, not by direct measurement. Zero retired colour in any of the four.
favicon.do_not: Do NOT rebuild a favicon from mo_ring_mark_on_light.svg or mo_ring_mark_on_dark.svg. Those are the full variant: 1px hairlines at 0.28 opacity, which vanish at 32px and below. That mistake is what produced the retired-eye favicon lingering beside correct ring-mark PNGs.

signal_line.rule: The breach segment must actually breach the dashed threshold. It is a diagram, not a squiggle.

commit_order: 2. Commit design-tokens.json, which carries the manifest shape with file paths.
4. node mo_visual_kit.js preflight - it resolves every mark and every font before writing anything.

HISTORICAL NOTE: step 3 formerly instructed a commit of the v3 kit over the templates/ copy. Both of those files were deleted on 2026-09-14 when the two diverged kits were merged into one. Corrected 2026-09-16. The old filenames are described rather than written, so a grep for them returns only real references.
marks.canonical_dir_note: Verified against the repo 2026-09-14: this is where the eleven variants live, and it is what the loaders resolve to (mo-tokens.js walks up from producers/, so the relative paths below are correct). 06_Brand_Assets/marks/ is the OLDER folder holding three pre-variant files and is NOT canonical. Two marks directories now exist; the legacy one should be emptied once every producer resolves by name.
marks.metadata_rule: A mark file is geometry only. If an SVG arrives carrying a <metadata> block — provenance manifests, editor cruft — strip it before committing. Each injected manifest is ~7.8KB against ~380 bytes of geometry, the producer base64-embeds the whole file at render time, and a re-download rewrites the manifest with fresh UUIDs so git reports every mark as modified. Strip: sed -i 's|<metadata>.*</metadata>||g' *.svg

committed.note: All ten present. The 2026-09-14 work order reported only a light variant existing; it had read the LEGACY 06_Brand_Assets/marks/ folder (3 files) rather than this one. mo_ring_mark_on_dark.svg already matches the spec that work order asked to be created.

A silent default that is right once and wrong four times is the same failure class as the font fallback that produced the blank card.

newsletter_issue.rule: The Signal carries its issue number wherever it is named. The newsletter entry above is a TEMPLATE, not a literal: {issue} is interpolated. A the_signal render without an issue number fails.
newsletter_issue.format: ISSUE then the integer, middot-separated, uppercase: THE SIGNAL · ISSUE 105. Middot per §5, never an em dash.
newsletter_issue.anchor: Issue 101 = 2026-08-21, the rebrand issue. Weekly, published Friday, and the counter never restarts. The Signal is a continuing publication (first issue 21 Feb 2024, over 100 before the rebrand), which is why it starts at 101 and why 01 is always wrong.
newsletter_issue.derivable: The number is CHECKABLE, not remembered: the anchor plus weekly cadence gives it. 101 + 4 weeks = 105 on 2026-09-18, which is the number Al gave. Independently corroborated at 102 = 2026-08-28 by a live LinkedIn first comment ("Read The Signal, issue 102"). Two fixed points and a cadence, so a wrong number is arithmetic, not opinion.
newsletter_issue.floor: eyebrowFor throws below 101. That is the gate that catches a restart at 01 — the failure The_Signal_Card_Standard.md called out and no producer enforced.
newsletter_issue.producer_note: The template lives HERE. mo-tokens.js eyebrowFor() interpolates it; mo_visual_kit.js blogthumb REQUIRES --issue for the_signal and composes the eyebrow rather than accepting one. The defect this closes: --eyebrow was free text and its gate only proved an eyebrow had been PASSED, so a hand-typed "THE SIGNAL" satisfied it and shipped a numberless card. Presence, not correctness — the same failure class as the eyebrow that defaulted to THE OBSERVABILITY DIGEST.

eyebrow_vocabulary.choice_rule: LENGTH AND TREATMENT decide it, not topic. Short and to the point is BYTE-SIZE. A larger technical explainer carrying diagrams is TECHNICAL. So a short post on a technical subject takes BYTE-SIZE.
eyebrow_vocabulary.worked_example: what-is-grafana-alloy is BYTE-SIZE. It is a technical subject, but it is written short and to the point, and length is what decides.
eyebrow_vocabulary.required: Required on every render, no default. A missing eyebrow fails the render rather than guessing.

fonts.rule: librsvg ignores @font-face entirely. SVG text renders through fontconfig, so the STATIC TTFs must be installed system-wide. Embedding a font in the SVG does nothing.
fonts.acceptance: fc-list "Montserrat:style=ExtraBold" returns at least one match. NOT a grep of bare fc-list output: under correct RIBBI naming fontconfig prints parallel comma lists ("Montserrat,Montserrat ExtraBold:style=ExtraBold,Regular"), in which the literal substring "Montserrat:style=ExtraBold" never appears. The old acceptance encoded the OLD non-compliant naming and started failing because the fonts were fixed properly. ASK fontconfig with a pattern; do not grep it. On Windows there is no fc-list, so the acceptance test is a rendered card with words on it in the right faces.
fonts.trap: Variable-font and per-optical-size downloads declare the wrong family name — "Montserrat Thin", "DM Sans 9pt" — so fontconfig never matches the family the producer asks for. Download the static TTFs.
fonts.silent_failure: A font-family fallback stack means a missing face renders in Liberation Sans instead of failing. Every producer must call assertFonts() before its first render.

name_table_defect.cause: UPSTREAM Google Fonts defect in the statics generated from the variable fonts. Verified against the binaries published as @fontsource/montserrat@5 and @fontsource/dm-sans@5: Montserrat-ExtraBold.ttf arrives declaring family "Montserrat Thin ExtraBold", Montserrat-Bold.ttf "Montserrat Thin", DMSans-*.ttf "DM Sans 9pt". RE-DOWNLOADING IS NOT A FIX — there is no clean upstream copy.
name_table_defect.effect: font-family:'Montserrat' matches nothing. Linux substitutes a fallback; Windows has nothing to substitute and DROPS the text, producing a flawless wordless card at exit code 0.
name_table_defect.fix: producers/normalise_font_names.py rewrites name IDs 1, 2, 4, 6, 16, 17 only. IDs 16/17 are the point: 1/2 can only express the four RIBBI styles, so a weight like ExtraBold has no legal home there. Setting 16=Montserrat / 17=ExtraBold is what makes a bare family request resolve. Of 19 tables in Montserrat-ExtraBold.ttf only name and head differ after a run; glyf, loca, hmtx, cmap and OS/2 are byte-identical.
name_table_defect.two_font_trees: Fonts exist byte-identical at 06_Brand_Assets/fonts/ and the repo root fonts/. Normalise BOTH or the stale copy drifts back.
name_table_defect.windows_install: NORMALISING THE REPO FILES IS NOT SUFFICIENT. The renderer reads the WINDOWS FONT STORE, not the repo folder. Installed copies cannot be overwritten — the font cache holds them open — and rewriting the registry names while the files stay stale gives correct names pointing at wrong files, which looks fixed and is not. Install under NEW filenames (-mo.ttf) and repoint the registry, remove the old-named entries, then RESTART THE SHELL because the font cache is read at process start.
name_table_defect.regresses: Every time anyone refreshes the fonts, because upstream is wrong at source. Run normalise_font_names.py --check before any render sweep. This estate has no CI, so --check in the runbook is the standing gate.

fonts.probe_limitation: assertFontsProbe compares two renders, so it detects SUBSTITUTION (family absent). It does NOT detect SYNTHESIS, and it does NOT detect a mislabelled name table. A pass proves the tool ran, not that the display face is real. Render one card and look.
fonts.gate_history: assertFonts grepped fc-list output against /Family:style=Style/ until 2026-09-14. That passed on Windows (no fc-list, returns skipped) and hard-broke Linux and CI after normalisation — the exact mirror of the defect it exists to catch. Raised by Content Management. A gate whose pass condition encodes a defect will fail when the defect is fixed.

gates.rule: If a check reads something other than the artefact that ships, it is theatre. Every resolver throws rather than falling back.
order: assertFonts() — before first render. Fonts resolve through fontconfig, not @font-face.
assertNoRetired(source) — at load. The producer carries no retired hex.
assertRenderClean(markup) — immediately before rasterising. Decodes every data: URI. Lives inside the render call so it cannot be skipped.
assertFilesClean(paths) — for assets read rather than embedded.
gates.preflight: node mo_visual_kit.js preflight — runs every gate, writes nothing.

surface_aliases.note: Surface name -> CANVAS/MODE name. This estate carried two names for one thing: blog_og is the lockup-lane name, og_card the canvas name. That was invisible while blogthumb hardcoded "og_card" for its size and "blog_og" for its lockup separately; the moment the producer resolved both from the real surface, T.size('blog_og') threw. Found by test, 2026-09-14.
surface_aliases.why_not_duplicate: byte_size and monthly_digest were briefly given their own canvas entries of [1200,630]. That was reverted: two canvas entries for one canvas is exactly how the two names arose. An alias is one declared fact; a duplicate is two facts that can drift.
surface_aliases.the_signal_defect: ADDED 2026-09-18. the_signal had NO canvas entry and NO alias, so T.size('the_signal') threw — while mo_visual_kit.js advertised the surface in its usage line AND in both of its required-flag error messages. The surface has therefore never rendered through the v3 producer; it died one line after the flag gates. Found by probing the reader rather than reading the usage string. Aliased to the existing, correctly-named signal_masthead canvas rather than given a duplicate [1200,630] entry, per why_not_duplicate.
surface_aliases.reading: mo-tokens resolves aliases inside size() and modeFor() ONLY. variantFor() does not alias, because dual-mode is a property of the surface rather than the canvas. lockupFor() does not alias either, because lane membership is a property of the surface — og_card is listed in house_lane in its own right.
